item.title: How 'the algorithm' works — and the $25 billion Meta judgment behind the explainer
item.description:
If you've ever wondered why your feed keeps showing you more of the same, the short answer is that 'the algorithm' is a set of rules built on millions of data points — your comments, reactions, shares, views, and how long you linger — used to predict what you're most likely to watch next. The more data it gets, the better its guesses, which is why one video watched leads to three more just like it, and why marketers can target ads so precisely.

The explainer lands against a major legal backdrop: Meta has had a rough year in court over exactly this data mining. New Mexico's case grew out of the Cambridge Analytica scandal, in which a researcher's Facebook quiz harvested data from quiz-takers and their friends, data that ended up with a political firm for targeted ads. A jury agreed Facebook misled users about their control over their data, and this week a judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion. Meta, calling the case 'a tax on speech,' plans to appeal.

Sources

  • The Pour Over: How’s “the Algorithm” Work? And What Is It?

item.title: Deadly school shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon
item.description:
Three children, ages 5, 8, and 11, and one teacher were killed in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon on Thursday. A 16-year-old former special-needs student hopped the school fence with a shotgun, shot through a locked door, and fired 15 or more rounds inside a classroom for students with special needs. Another student and teacher were seriously injured and are in stable condition.

A 36-year-old father who saw the suspect breaking into the school followed him inside and shot and killed the shooter before police arrived minutes later; officials praised the father and a school staffer for their heroism. Authorities believe the teen obtained the shotgun from his mother and are still investigating a motive. The tragedy will reignite debate over school security and teen access to firearms.

Sources

  • The Pour Over: Oregon School Shooting
